text:
frances: Hit a weird onboarding snag: rotated a project key, updated REDWOOD_API_KEY in my shell, but the running sample-service kept 401ing.

tony: did you have a creds file or any other REDWOOD_* envs set? quick debug output helps.

frances: no REDWOOD_TOKEN set explicitly. Logs show resolver picked up a file: ~/.redwood/creds and returned that token (masked). I did `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=proj_live_new123` before starting.

sam: parity bug we've seen: some SDKs historically prefer disk file over env, and some cache at startup. If a creds file appears later or the process has a cached token, env updates get ignored.

frances: minimal repro I ran: 
```
rm -f ~/.redwood/creds
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=proj_live_new123
node samples/service.js
# then write old creds file into ~/.redwood/creds
printf "token=proj_live_old456" > ~/.redwood/creds
# subsequent requests still use old token
```

tony: bleh. Proposed immediate fixes: 1) Make resolver check process.env for REDWOOD_API_KEY on each request (cheap) 2) when env differs from cached token, invalidate cache and clear any auth headers in pooled clients 3) emit a masked startup warning if both env and creds file exist and differ.

security-jen: logging must mask tokens and only show last 4 chars. Also add a security note in the deprecation doc for alternate env names (REDWOOD_TOKEN) to avoid accidental exposure during debug.

frances: short-term workaround for others: `unset REDWOOD_TOKEN && rm -f ~/.redwood/creds && restart`. I added that to the sample-service README.

sam: mid-term: normalize env var names across SDKs to REDWOOD_API_KEY, deprecate REDWOOD_TOKEN with clear migration warnings, and publish a small CLI flag `--no-write` so onboarding can avoid writing creds to disk by default.

ton y: (typo) tony: also add a small integration test in sample CI that simulates rotation: start with env set, trigger creds file change, and assert next request uses new env key.

devex-bot: Reminder: file an issue in repo redwood/sdk-cred and tag @eng-runtime, @devex, and @security.

frances: filed #1203 with repro and logs. I'll open a patch that logs the token source (masked) on first request and invalidates cache on env mismatch.

sam: sounds good. After the patch we should sweep quickstarts and docker compose examples to avoid copying ~/.redwood into images. That has been a frequent footgun.

security-jen: also add a short KB on safe rotation: 1) update key in secrets manager 2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY 3) restart processes or send SIGHUP 4) validate with a smoke request.

frances: thanks all, fixing docs + PR incoming.
